# L10: Storyboard first, then let Claude edit (pause-and-play teardown)

Chanyoung Ryu "Chandler" (@chandlerintelligence) · ig-reel · https://www.instagram.com/p/DfAMeazmN77/ · notes: [lessons/10_storyboard-first-claude-edit.md](../../brain/lessons/10_storyboard-first-claude-edit.md)

**Core lesson:** Before Claude edits (or you shoot), have it write the whole video as a storyboard table of line, on-screen element, tool and sound cue, agree on it, then build. Shown as a pause-and-play breakdown of a $97 workflow with recipes for text behind the head, shadowed captions, a moody FFmpeg grade and a whip pan.


## Ideas from this source (15)

- **[Storyboard table before any edit](../topics/process.md#l10-storyboard-before-edit)** · process: Before Claude touches the footage (he does it even before shooting), it writes the whole video as a table: every line, what is on screen, which tool makes it. You fix the plan and agree on it, then Claude builds the edit from it. Chandler's columns: # / Freeze (time) / Chandler says / On screen.
- **[SCORE and EMPHASIS lines per beat](../topics/sound.md#l10-storyboard-score-emphasis)** · sound: The source creator's storyboard ("claude-editing / storyboard, v2, 24 beats") gives each beat timecodes, duration, shot type, the spoken line, a direction, an EMPHASIS line (which word goes gold serif, which is struck through) and a SCORE line with music cues such as "drop 1 on 'Claude did.'" and "tape stop under the scratch 0:28.3, drop 2 on 'storyboard'".
- **[Half-second music dropout after the punchline](../topics/sound.md#l10-dropout-after-punchline)** · sound: Right after the hook line "Claude did." the whole mix drops to near-silence (-42 LUFS) for about 0.5 s at 2.50 s, then the beat returns. The rest of the 85 s has no silence at all.
- **[Pause-and-play breakdown of a reel](../topics/ideas.md#l10-pause-and-play-breakdown)** · ideas: Play another creator's popular or paid reel with its audio in a rounded card. Freeze it at each effect, shrink it to a thumbnail beside your head, explain how to make that effect, then play on. In L10 the source plays 10 times, 19.9 s of 85 s (23%), and its own lines carry the story.

- **[Text behind your head](../topics/effects.md#l10-text-behind-head)** · effects: Cut the speaker out with a person-segmentation model and put words on a layer between the background and the person, so the title sits behind the head. - **[Demo each effect on your own shot](../topics/effects.md#l10-apply-effect-on-yourself)** · effects: Each technique is applied to his own footage as he names it: grade-panel sliders move and his saturation measurably drops (SATAVG ~8 to ~4.5 at 56 s), his shot shrinks into the centre of the 3x3 wall, the words go behind his head.
